items.note: It answers the question directly. Pro churn rose after July, while Basic, the control, stayed low. The increase "likely contributed," but the data can't prove it caused the churn. The figures check out: 1 Pro cancellation before July; 8 cancellations in Aug–Sep from the 16 accounts that signed up before July; and 2 of the 4 July signups also cancelled.
The counts leave out all trial accounts: 20 Pro and 20 Basic remain, and none of the trial cancellations are counted.
The 5 qa*@ourco.test accounts are left out. The Pro total of 20, with 4 July signups, matches the data after removing them.
It says a cancel_month means the account churned and a blank one means it's still active.
There's a summary section aimed at the CEO in fairly plain language. It still uses some analyst jargon, though ("logo rate," "MRR," "at-risk accounts").
The summary itself has 5 bullets, but before it comes a 6-item data-quality section and an assumptions paragraph. So the whole deliverable is much longer than a summary of at most 5 bullets.
It suggests one chart: a line chart of monthly Pro vs Basic churn rate for Apr–Sep, with a marker at July and a count on each point.
It rates confidence "moderate-to-low" and explains why: the counts are very small (1 vs 8 cancellations).
